title: Natural Domain and Range of a Radical with a Linear Radicand
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the natural domain and range of the real-valued function F(x) = sqrt(5x + 10).

steps.title: Set Up the Radicand Inequality
steps.explanation: To produce real outputs from the square root function, the linear radicand 5x + 10 must be greater than or equal to zero.
steps.why: The principal square root of a negative quantity is not a real number.

steps.title: Solve the Linear Inequality for x
steps.explanation: Subtract 10 from both sides to obtain 5x >= -10, then divide both sides by 5 to isolate x >= -2.
steps.why: Dividing both sides of an inequality by a positive constant preserves the inequality direction.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: The natural domain includes the left endpoint x = -2, where the radicand vanishes, together with all real numbers greater than -2.
steps.why: Closed brackets denote inclusion of the endpoint where the radical evaluates to zero.

steps.title: Determine the Range
steps.explanation: At x = -2, F(-2) = sqrt(0) = 0. As x increases toward infinity, 5x + 10 increases without bound, so F(x) attains every non-negative real value in [0, inf).
steps.why: The principal square root maps [0, inf) continuously onto [0, inf).
